sample.universe: All Danish households in administrative registers spanning 1980-2011; the data cover the entire adult Danish population
sample.unit_of_observation: Family member (or coworker) by year, with event time t = year - tau measured relative to the shock year; standard errors clustered at the household level (workplace level for the coworker analysis)
selection_rules: Primary setting: all households in which an individual experienced a heart attack or a stroke for the first time and survived for the four-year analysis horizon (Delta = 5)

Treatment group: family members of individuals shocked in year tau; control group: family members, from the same cohort group Omega, of individuals who experience the same shock at tau + 5, assigned a placebo shock at t = 0
Spouses identified from register matches of all married and cohabiting couples prior to the shock
Adult children identified from parent-child matches, available for individuals born after 1960
Children-in-law identified as the spouses of those adult children

Close coworkers: from the pre-shock periods t = -4 to t = -1, coworkers in workplaces at or below the sample's 25th percentile of size (about 20 employees), in a similar occupation class (Statistics Denmark/ISCO classification), with an age gap of 5 years or less; coworkers who are also family members are excluded
Distant coworkers: workers in the same workplace who are distant along at least one of workplace size, age gap, or occupation class
Secondary setting of death events: all families in which a member died between 1985 and 2011, with spouses and children constructed in the same way
Cholesterol blood-test outcomes are available only for the subset of the sample residing in Greater Copenhagen
Equations (4) and (5) are estimated on treated (bereaved) households only, divided by cause of death; for the cross-condition columns the competing condition is excluded from the comparison group
sample.period: Registers span 1980-2011 (prescription drugs 1995-2011; health insurance contacts 1985-2011; inpatient hospitalizations 1980-2011; outpatient 1994-2011; causes of death from 1980 onward); the death-event sample covers deaths 1985-2011
sample.n_observations: Not reported for the pooled data; estimation samples range from 43,664 (Table 3, column 3) to 2,922,141 (Table 4, column 2) observations

construction_notes: Time is normalized as t = year - tau, where tau is the year of the actual shock for the treatment group and of the assigned placebo shock for the control group; the control group's actual shock occurs at t = Delta = 5
Delta = 5 is chosen so that effects can be identified up to four years after the shock; local perturbations to Delta are reported in online Appendix Table 8
All monetary values of health care expenditure are in nominal Danish kroner deflated to 2000 prices using the consumer price index; in 2000 the exchange rate was approximately DKK 8 per US$1

Statin consumption is measured as an indicator from the Prescription Drug Database using the ATC classification; smoking-cessation medication is ATC code N07BA (including nicotine replacement therapies)
Opioid consumption uses the WHO 'defined daily dose' (DDD) standardization of prescribed amounts into day equivalents

Cardiovascular risk is predicted from a probit model for the one-year probability of a first heart attack or stroke estimated on the entire adult population, with age fixed effects, gender, year fixed effects, education, and lagged hypertension and diabetes statuses proxied by condition-specific prescribed medications; spouses are split at the population median of the predicted probability in t = -1
Occupation classes follow Statistics Denmark's official classification based on ISCO (managers versus non-managers, and non-managers by required skill level low/medium/high)
Distance between in-law households is the straight-line length between municipality centroids under post-2007 definitions (98 municipalities); the sample median distance is 22 kilometers (14 miles)
Outpatient hospital contact for having a family member with a history of cancer is ICD-10 code Z80
Female cancers comprise ovarian, cervical, and breast cancer

Unless otherwise indicated, X_{i,t} contains age fixed effects, calendar year fixed effects, gender, and education; standard errors are robust and clustered at the household level (workplace level in Table 2)

population.description: Prime-age spouses (ages 25-55) of individuals who experienced a first-time nonfatal heart attack or stroke and survived the four-year analysis horizon
population.period: Shocks observed over the register period 1980-2011; statin outcomes are available from the Prescription Drug Database 1995-2011
population.selection: Households are included only if a member experienced a first-time heart attack or stroke and that member survived the four-year analysis horizon (Delta = 5); control households are those in which the same shock occurs five years later, drawn from the same cohort group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the realization of the shock, the outcomes of the treatment group and of the control group (families that experience the same shock five years later) would have run parallel.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Pre-shock event-study coefficients delta_r for r < 0 are reported in every dynamic table and plotted in the figures; the paper reads them as showing virtually no differential pre-trends.

formal.as_written: Validation of the parallel trends assumption requires that delta_r = 0 for all r < 0.

key_assumptions.assumption: Within a window of length Delta, the particular year in which the severe health shock occurs is as good as random, so shock timing is unrelated to the family members' counterfactual health behavior given cohort, age and calendar year.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper argues heart attacks and strokes are sudden and severe events whose particular timing is likely unpredictable, and points to the absence of differential pre-trends.

key_assumptions.assumption: Control households do not respond, within the four-year analysis horizon, to their own shock that arrives at tau + Delta; the horizon is cut at four years precisely because the control group becomes treated in period Delta = 5.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The design restricts the analysis horizon to four years because the control group becomes 'treated' in period Delta; no separate anticipation test is reported.

key_assumptions.assumption: The primary sample is conditioned on the shocked individual surviving the four-year analysis horizon, so the estimates are for surviving-shock households only.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as a sample-construction rule; the paper does not test whether survival selection matters.

threats_discussed: Control-group family members experience the same shock at a later age, which generates a systematic level difference between treatment and control groups.
Treatment and control groups could differ in their expectations over the particular year of the shock within the chosen window.
Statin take-up could reflect treatment of family members' own newly induced conditions rather than preventive investment.
A family physician shared across household members could aggregate information and drive the apparent spillover.

Greater valuation of the sick spouse's health through realized household income risk, child-rearing considerations, or caregiving needs could drive the response rather than the family member's own health behavior.
robustness_checks: Pre-shock event-time coefficients delta_r for r < 0 reported and read as showing no differential trends.
Local perturbations to Delta give similar results (online Appendix Table 8).
An alternative control group matched on observable pre-shock risk factors gives similar findings (online Appendix Table 9).
No increase in the incidence of own cardiovascular shocks or of hospital contacts of any type among spouses or children (online Appendix Table 7).
Similar-magnitude responses in households where husbands and wives do not share the same doctor (online Appendix Table 4).
Responses do not vary with whether the sick person was the primary earner, with the presence of younger children, or with shock severity measured by hospitalization days (online Appendix Table 3).
unresolved_confounders: All the shocks studied can have various health effects on family members, for example on mental health through stress induced by the adverse family health event.

The family members' own physicians can act as a mechanism, for example by learning of the relative's shock and recommending preventive care; the paper does not separate this from the family members' own behavior.

ambiguities: The column reports nine event-time coefficients (delta_-4 to delta_4). This claim records the coefficient at the single horizon the paper's own text highlights; the other event-time coefficients in the same column are different quantities, not disagreements.
The paper prints no significance stars and no p-values, so statistical significance is read off the coefficient-to-standard-error ratio.

The baseline recorded here is the counterfactual printed for t = 4 (14.87631 DDD), matching the horizon of the coefficient; the paper's own text anchors the magnitude on the counterfactual at t = 0 (9.74366 DDD).
Figure 3 prints no observation counts.

evidence.annotation: Panel D. Opioid dosage. Printed on the panel: coefficient at t = 4 is -0.93168 (0.29347); Counterfactual at t = 0: 9.74366; Counterfactual at t = 4: 14.87631; Coefficient on treat_i: 0.49134 (0.22850).

evidence.how: Coefficient -0.93168 divided by its printed standard error 0.29347 gives a ratio of about -3.17, above conventional two-sided critical values in absolute value.
